findings.title: GitHub user verification is skipped entirely for installations without an existing Integration
findings.body: When no Integration row exists for the installation_id, the code returns `pipeline.next_step()` immediately. The new check that the OAuth-authenticated GitHub login matches `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` only runs when the Integration already exists (line ~501). If the installation webhook has not yet created the Integration, or the flow is reached in another order, the pipeline proceeds with no check that the authenticated user installed the app. That makes the OAuth step ineffective in exactly the path it is meant to guard, so an attacker could complete installation with an installation_id they do not own.

findings.title: KeyError when the existing Integration has no 'sender' metadata
findings.body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes the key exists. `build_integration` only stores `sender` when `state.get("sender")` is truthy, and integrations created by other paths or before this field existed will not have it. For such an ACTIVE integration the check raises KeyError and the setup request returns a 500 instead of the intended error page. Use a safe lookup and fail closed with the error response.

findings.title: Network failure in OAuth token exchange is not handled
findings.body: `safe_urlopen` is called outside the try block that protects only `safe_urlread`. If GitHub is unreachable or the request times out, the exception propagates and the user gets a 500 rather than the 'Invalid installation request' error page used for every other failure in this view. Wrap the request in the same error handling, or return `error(...)` on exception.

findings.title: Test for installation-not-found no longer exercises the not-found path
findings.body: The original assertion checked for 'The GitHub installation could not be found.' from the 404 branch in `build_integration`. The test now sends a mismatched state, so it fails earlier with 'Invalid installation request.' and the 404 branch has no coverage. The test name no longer matches what it checks. Restore the original 404 scenario and add a separate state-mismatch test.
